_: The Scenarios domain catalog: every factor a scenario may use hangs off one of these nodes. status: category (a heading), measured (observed now, with a source), estimated (effect known from research or a stated heuristic), emerging (not real at scale yet; carries a horizon and a chance it becomes real), speculative (claimed, weakly evidenced). A factor can be labeled weaker than its domain, never stronger. Notes are short and hedged; a source is where to check, not proof.

domains.name: Body: physiological state
domains.note: What the body brings to the task right now.

domains.name: Sleep debt
domains.note: Hours short of need over recent nights. Around 17 to 19 hours awake, some tasks degrade about as much as at a blood alcohol level of 0.05%.
domains.source: Williamson & Feyer 2000, Occupational and Environmental Medicine; Dawson & Reid 1997, Nature

domains.name: Physical fatigue
domains.note: Exertion accumulated within a shift; slows movement and raises error and injury risk.

domains.name: Heat strain
domains.note: Core temperature rise under load and protective gear; judgment and endurance fall as it climbs.
domains.source: ACGIH heat stress threshold limit values; NFPA 1584 rehabilitation standard

domains.name: Hydration
domains.note: About 2% of body mass lost to sweat impairs endurance and some thinking tasks.
domains.source: American College of Sports Medicine position stand, 2007

domains.name: Aerobic fitness
domains.note: Higher VO2max sustains work under load for longer.

domains.name: Strength
domains.note: Reserve for lifts, drags and carries; less reserve means earlier fatigue.

domains.name: Fuel
domains.note: Long gaps without food lower sustained attention for many people.

domains.name: Caffeine
domains.note: Improves alertness and reaction time when sleep-deprived; the effect shrinks with daily use.
domains.source: McLellan, Caldwell & Lieberman 2016, Neuroscience & Biobehavioral Reviews

domains.name: Injury or pain
domains.note: Pain competes for attention and limits range of motion.

domains.name: Illness
domains.note: Even a mild illness lowers work capacity and mood.

domains.name: Heart-rate reserve used
domains.note: Share of heart-rate reserve in use; read directly from a wearable.

domains.name: Age
domains.note: Changes recovery time and heat tolerance on average; individuals vary widely.

domains.name: Mind: psychological and cognitive state
domains.note: What the head brings to the task right now.

domains.name: Stress and arousal
domains.note: Moderate arousal can help simple tasks and hurt complex ones. The inverted U (Yerkes-Dodson) is a useful heuristic with mixed evidence, not a law.

domains.name: Self-efficacy
domains.note: Belief in one's capability predicts effort and persistence.
domains.source: Bandura 1977, Psychological Review

domains.name: Motivation
domains.note: Drives whether effort starts and how long it lasts.

domains.name: Attention
domains.note: Divided attention slows responses and raises misses.

domains.name: Cognitive load
domains.note: Working memory holds roughly four chunks; overload shows up as skipped steps.
domains.source: Cowan 2001, Behavioral and Brain Sciences

domains.name: Mood
domains.note: Self-rated in a check-in: a measurement of what the person reports, not a diagnosis.

domains.name: Energy
domains.note: Self-rated in a check-in.

domains.name: Risk tolerance
domains.note: Shapes which option looks acceptable under uncertainty.

domains.name: Threat perception
domains.note: Narrows attention (tunnel vision) and speeds simple responses; slows complex decisions.

domains.name: Decision fatigue
domains.note: The ego-depletion effect behind it failed a large multi-lab replication; treat it as a hypothesis.
domains.source: Hagger et al. 2016, Perspectives on Psychological Science

domains.name: Habit strength
domains.note: Automaticity grows over weeks; one study found a median near 66 days with a wide range.
domains.source: Lally et al. 2010, European Journal of Social Psychology

domains.name: Spirit: meaning, values and faith
domains.note: What a person is working for.

domains.name: Sense of purpose
domains.note: Linked with persistence and wellbeing in observational studies.

domains.name: Faith practice
domains.note: Regular religious practice is associated with lower depression and higher wellbeing in large cohorts; observational, so not proof of cause.
domains.source: VanderWeele and colleagues, Human Flourishing Program, Harvard

domains.name: Gratitude practice
domains.note: Small positive effects on wellbeing in trials.

domains.name: Values fit
domains.note: Work that matches stated values tends to be sustained longer.

domains.name: Skill: expertise and training
domains.note: What practice has built.

domains.name: Experience
domains.note: Years in the role.

domains.name: Days since last drill
domains.note: Unused skills decay; procedural skills hold better than thinking skills.
domains.source: Arthur et al. 1998, Human Performance

domains.name: Certification level
domains.note: Formal qualification held.

domains.name: Familiarity with this task or place
domains.note: Known ground and known equipment save time.

domains.name: Team: topology and coordination
domains.note: Who works together and how.

domains.name: Team size
domains.note: Communication links grow as n(n-1)/2: more hands, more coordination cost.
domains.source: Brooks 1975 (a heuristic)

domains.name: Cohesion
domains.note: Crews that have worked together make fewer coordination errors.

domains.name: Communication quality
domains.note: Closed-loop communication cuts missed and duplicated actions.

domains.name: Leadership clarity
domains.note: One clear decision-maker speeds action.

domains.name: Role clarity
domains.note: Known assignments before arrival save the first minutes.

domains.name: Skill mix
domains.note: Coverage of the skills the task needs.

domains.name: Span of control
domains.note: Incident command guidance keeps it between 3 and 7, ideally 5.
domains.source: National Incident Management System, Incident Command System

domains.name: Handoff quality
domains.note: Information lost at shift change or between people.

domains.name: Task: what is being done
domains.note: The demands of the work itself.

domains.name: Complexity
domains.note: More steps, more places to slip.

domains.name: Time available
domains.note: The clock the task runs against.

domains.name: Required speed
domains.note: Speed and accuracy trade off against each other.

domains.name: Precision required
domains.note: Tighter tolerance, slower safe pace.

domains.name: Coordination demand
domains.note: How many people must act in step.

domains.name: Physical load
domains.note: Weight carried or moved.

domains.name: Distance to cover
domains.note: Travel or carry distance.

domains.name: Novelty
domains.note: First time doing it, or in this setting.

domains.name: Interruptions
domains.note: Interruptions raise error rates in procedural work.

domains.name: Time: when it happens
domains.note: The clock and the calendar.

domains.name: Time of day
domains.note: Hour of the day, 0 to 23.

domains.name: Circadian low
domains.note: Errors and accidents peak in the early-morning trough (about 02:00 to 06:00) for shift workers.
domains.source: Folkard & Tucker 2003, Occupational Medicine

domains.name: Day of week
domains.note: Weekly rhythms in traffic, calls and energy.

domains.name: Season
domains.note: Heat, cold, daylight and holidays.

domains.name: Hours on duty
domains.note: Risk rises after about 12 hours on shift.
domains.source: Folkard & Tucker 2003, Occupational Medicine

domains.name: Time since last rest
domains.note: Hours since the last real break.

domains.name: Environment: physical conditions
domains.note: The place and the weather.

domains.name: Air temperature
domains.note: Dry-bulb temperature.

domains.name: Heat index or WBGT
domains.note: Wet-bulb globe temperature is the working standard for heat stress.
domains.source: National Weather Service; OSHA heat guidance

domains.name: Humidity
domains.note: High humidity blocks sweat cooling.

domains.name: Cold stress
domains.note: Cold slows hands and judgment.

domains.name: Light and visibility
domains.note: Darkness, smoke or glare.

domains.name: Noise
domains.note: Loud noise impairs speech and some thinking tasks.

domains.name: Air quality or smoke
domains.note: Particulates and gases.

domains.name: Terrain
domains.note: Stairs, slope, footing, obstacles.

domains.name: Precipitation and storms
domains.note: Rain, snow, ice, lightning.

domains.name: Wind
domains.note: Spreads fire and smoke, chills, slows movement.

domains.name: Altitude
domains.note: Less oxygen per breath above about 1,500 m.

domains.name: Traffic delay
domains.note: Minutes added to travel.

domains.name: Equipment and technology
domains.note: The tools in hand.

domains.name: Equipment reliability
domains.note: How often the tool works when needed.

domains.name: Gear weight
domains.note: Protective gear and breathing apparatus add tens of kilograms and trap heat.

domains.name: Radio and comms reliability
domains.note: Share of transmissions heard the first time.

domains.name: Tool familiarity
domains.note: Unfamiliar tools cost time and errors.

domains.name: Protective equipment fit
domains.note: Poor fit restricts movement and protection.

domains.name: AI assistance
domains.note: Present today; effects vary widely by task, and people over-trust it on tasks outside its competence.

domains.name: Money: resources
domains.note: What can be spent.

domains.name: Cash runway
domains.note: Months of costs covered.

domains.name: Budget
domains.note: Money set aside for this.

domains.name: Income stability
domains.note: Predictable income lowers stress and widens options.

domains.name: Cost of an error
domains.note: What a mistake costs.

domains.name: Debt load
domains.note: Payments owed against income.

domains.name: Information
domains.note: What is known, and how well.

domains.name: Data quality
domains.note: Accurate, current, complete.

domains.name: Uncertainty
domains.note: How much is unknown at decision time.

domains.name: News flow
domains.note: What the field sources report.

domains.name: Misinformation exposure
domains.note: False claims competing for attention.

domains.name: Feedback speed
domains.note: Fast feedback speeds learning; slow feedback breeds overconfidence.

domains.name: Social: people around
domains.note: Support and obligations.

domains.name: Social support
domains.note: People to lean on; buffers stress.

domains.name: Family obligations
domains.note: Time owed at home.

domains.name: Reputation and trust
domains.note: How much others extend credit.

domains.name: Community events
domains.note: Gatherings that change demand or traffic.

domains.name: Economy
domains.note: The money weather.

domains.name: Inflation
domains.note: Consumer price change.
domains.source: US Bureau of Labor Statistics CPI

domains.name: Interest rates
domains.note: Cost of borrowing.
domains.source: Federal Reserve

domains.name: Job market
domains.note: Ease of finding work.

domains.name: Housing costs
domains.note: Rent or mortgage.

domains.name: Market volatility
domains.note: Expected swings in stock prices.

domains.name: World: large-scale events
domains.note: What moves everyone at once.

domains.name: Public health events
domains.note: Outbreaks and their rules.

domains.name: Conflict and security
domains.note: Wars, unrest, cyberattacks.

domains.name: Policy and regulation
domains.note: Laws and rules that change the task.

domains.name: Supply chains
domains.note: Parts and goods arriving late.

domains.name: Climate trend
domains.note: Hot extremes are observed to be more frequent; projections carry ranges.
domains.source: IPCC Sixth Assessment Report, Working Group I

domains.name: Technology adoption
domains.note: How widely a tool is in use.

domains.name: Cosmos: planet and space
domains.note: Seen and unseen forces from beyond the weather.

domains.name: Space weather
domains.note: Strong geomagnetic storms degrade HF radio and GPS accuracy; VHF and UHF public-safety radio is rarely affected.
domains.source: NOAA Space Weather Prediction Center scales

domains.name: Solar cycle phase
domains.note: Cycle 25 reached its maximum period around 2024-2025; strong storms stay more likely for a few years after.
domains.source: NASA and NOAA, October 2024

domains.name: Daylight hours
domains.note: Short days shift sleep and mood for some people.

domains.name: Lunar phase as a cause of behavior
domains.note: The phase itself is measured. The popular belief that full moons make nights busier has not held up in controlled studies of emergency volume.

domains.name: Cosmic rays
domains.note: Cause rare bit flips in electronics; no meaningful effect on people at ground level.

domains.name: Asteroid impact risk
domains.note: Tracked by NASA; the chance of a damaging impact in any given year is tiny.

domains.name: Emerging: factors that are not real at scale yet
domains.note: Kept apart so a future factor is never read as a present fact. Each carries a horizon and a chance it becomes real.

domains.name: AI agents doing whole tasks at work
domains.note: Agents that act, not only answer, inside everyday work; changes who does what on a team.

domains.name: Real-time biosensor coaching
domains.note: Wearables that read heat strain and fatigue and warn in the moment.

domains.name: Humanoid robots on crews
domains.note: Machines that carry, search or hold a line beside people.

domains.name: Autonomous vehicles in daily traffic
domains.note: Changes delay and crash patterns on response routes.

domains.name: Brain-computer interfaces for healthy users
domains.note: Direct neural input and output outside medicine.

domains.name: Quantum computers breaking today's public-key encryption
domains.note: Would expose data encrypted today with RSA or elliptic curves; post-quantum standards (NIST, 2024) are the migration path.

domains.name: Synthetic media at scale
domains.note: Cheap convincing fakes raise the cost of verifying anything seen or heard.

domains.name: Heat extremes of the 2040s
domains.note: Projected more frequent extreme-heat days; the size depends on emissions.

domains.name: Personal AI managing money
domains.note: Assistants that move money within limits a person sets.

domains.name: Gene or cell therapies that change performance
domains.note: Beyond treating disease; mostly unproven outside medicine.
